summary.headline: {{insurer}} rejected your {{amount}} claim

missing.policyStart: Your policy start date wasn't in your documents. It matters for waiting periods, so add your policy schedule or first policy if you have it.

meaning.pre_existing: The insurer says you had this illness before your policy began, and that it is still inside the waiting period for such illnesses. What counts is when it was first diagnosed or treated, so dates matter most.
meaning.specific_waiting_period: Some treatments are only covered after a fixed time with the insurer (for example 2 years for cataract). The insurer says that time hadn't passed yet.
meaning.initial_waiting_period: Most policies don't cover illness in the first 30 days, except accidents. The insurer says your claim falls in that window.
meaning.non_disclosure: The insurer says something about your health wasn't declared when you bought the policy. Insurers must show it actually mattered, and after 5 years of cover they usually can't use this reason at all.
meaning.room_rent: The insurer says your room cost more than your policy allows, so it cut your claim. Check your policy: many plans have no room limit.
meaning.reasonable_charges: The insurer says the hospital charged more than is usual and paid only part.
meaning.diagnostic_only: The insurer says you were admitted only for tests, which isn't covered. If you received treatment, that matters.
meaning.not_medically_necessary: The insurer says the hospital stay wasn't needed. Your doctor's notes are the key evidence.
meaning.excluded_treatment: The insurer says your policy excludes this treatment. The exact wording of the exclusion matters.
meaning.missing_documents: The insurer says it didn't get all the papers it needed. This is often the easiest to fix.
meaning.late_intimation: The insurer says it was told about the hospital stay too late. Delays for good reasons are often accepted.
meaning.sub_limit: The insurer says a limit in your policy was reached, so it paid only part.
meaning.under_24_hours: The insurer says your stay was under 24 hours. Many day-care procedures are still covered.

hearing.title: Hearing rehearsal
hearing.introSub: A live voice rehearsal with your real case. You'll get a score and a better answer after each reply.
hearing.roleInsurer: defends the rejection and pushes back
hearing.needAnalysis: Finish the case analysis first, so the rehearsal can use your facts.
hearing.tip1: Use the exact dates on your documents. Don't guess.
hearing.tip2: Stick to facts. If you don't know, say "I don't know".
hearing.tip3: Keep answers short — one or two sentences.

tracker.title: Case tracker

send.title: Send your appeal to the insurer
send.body: Email or post your appeal letter to the {{body}}. They have {{days}} days to reply. Tell us once it's sent and we'll track the deadline.

waiting.title: Waiting for a reply from: {{body}}
waiting.body: They should reply by {{date}}. If they don't, we'll tell you what to do next.
waiting.overdue: The reply is overdue. We'll move your case to the next step automatically.

next.title: Next: {{body}}
